title: The Borrowed Portrait
premise: When the coffin of town founder Nathaniel Grey is found empty during a centennial exhumation, retired detective Edmund Whitlock is dragged back into the work he fled a decade ago. The investigation peels back the town's founding myth: Grey never died here at all, and the portrait hanging in the town hall—the one every family claims as their heritage—is a forgery painted by a woman the town erased from its records. As Edmund follows the trail to the drowned village beneath the reservoir, they discover their own missing decade is tangled in the cover-up, and that the 'closed case' that broke them was manufactured to protect the town's borrowed identity. In the end, Edmund chooses truth over belonging, exposing the forgery and giving the erased painter her name back—finding, paradoxically, a real family among those willing to stand in the wreckage with them.
about_author: Silas Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing the paper trails of small coastal towns before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about the lies communities tell themselves, and the quiet people who keep the files.

chapters.title: The Exhumation
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. During the centennial ceremony, the founder's coffin is opened before the whole town—and it holds only river stones and a folded photograph. Edmund, now selling used books and avoiding eye contact, is recognized by the new mayor and asked, politely, to consult. The emotional beat is the sick lurch of being seen again after ten years of chosen invisibility.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund resists, but their old case files—kept obsessively in the bookshop's back room—contain a detail from the original 1974 death certificate that matches the photograph in the coffin. A break-in that night takes only one folder: the one about the Grey estate. Beat: the past refusing to stay filed, and Edmund's fear that they were always going to be pulled back in.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Frame
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, with an interleafed 1974 letter. Research into the town hall portrait reveals an X-ray layer beneath: a different face, a woman's, painted over. The letter, hidden in a donated book, is signed only 'V.' and speaks of 'borrowing a dead man's face.' Beat: wonder and unease—Edmund realizes the town's most sacred object is a lie.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore
chapters.summary: POV alternating Edmund and Mayor Ruth Calloway. Edmund interviews the three surviving town elders who closed the original case; each gives a slightly different account of the night Grey 'died.' Ruth pressures Edmund quietly to stop, offering the bookshop a lifeline grant. Beat: Edmund recognizes the shape of a cover-up—and the temptation of belonging if they just let it go.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The reservoir drops during a drought, exposing the ruins of Millbrook, the village flooded in 1975 to build the town's prosperity. Edmund finds a collapsed cottage with a studio: pigments, brushes, and a second portrait—an unfinished Grey, signed 'Vera Ashcombe.' Beat: grief and fury on behalf of the erased; the mystery now has a human face.

chapters.title: The Case That Closed Me
chapters.summary: POV Edmund in fragmented flashback. Ten years ago, Edmund closed a drowning case in the reservoir—a young man, ruled accidental—and it destroyed their career and marriage when they refused to sign off. The folder stolen from the bookshop was about that case. Beat: raw vulnerability; the empty coffin and the drowning are the same story.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Edmund and Ruth. Confrontation: Ruth admits the founders faked Grey's death to escape debts, flooded Millbrook to hide it, and let Vera Ashcombe paint the lie—then erased her when she threatened to confess. The drowning ten years ago was a descendant trying to raise the truth. Beat: the climax's moral hinge—Ruth offers Edmund a place in the town's future if the past stays drowned.

chapters.title: The Empty Frame
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Someone cuts the portrait from its frame in the town hall—the physical heart of the town's identity—framing Edmund for the vandalism. Arrested, then released, Edmund finds the town turning on them: the outsider who came back to burn the myth. Beat: isolation at its peak; Edmund has lost the belonging they were offered.

chapters.title: Vera
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, climax at the reservoir at dawn. The thief is the drowned man's sister, who has Vera's confession and the original Grey death record. Together they raise what the tide took—documents, bones, truth—and Edmund publicly presents the case no one wanted reopened. Beat: cathartic confrontation; Edmund chooses truth over the town's love, and the sister chooses to stand with them.

chapters.title: A New Shelf
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, months later. The town hall hangs Vera Ashcombe's restored portrait beside a plaque telling the real founding story; some townsfolk never forgive, but a found circle gathers in the bookshop—Ruth included, humbled. Edmund shelves a new section: local history, uncorrected. Beat: quiet resolution—belonging rebuilt on truth rather than myth, and Edmund no longer invisible by choice.
